overview.headline: Population genetics and how allele frequencies are described and grouped

keyPoints.point: Population genetics studies distribution and change in allele frequencies shaped by evolutionary forces
keyPoints.quote: distribution of and change in allele frequencies under the influence of the four evolutionary forces

keyPoints.point: Descriptive statistics summarize population data in a clear and concise manner for large collections
keyPoints.quote: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner.

keyPoints.point: In biology a population denotes a group that breeds primarily among themselves often due to physical isolation
keyPoints.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.

keyPoints.point: Racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of human genetic variation and ethnicity offers imperfect alternative
keyPoints.quote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species.

keyTerms.gloss: measure of distribution and frequency of different allele versions within a population
keyTerms.quote: distribution of and change in allele frequencies under the influence of the four evolutionary forces

keyTerms.gloss: evolutionary force where natural selection favors certain traits influencing allele change
keyTerms.quote: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration

keyTerms.gloss: evolutionary force where genetic drift causes random shifts in allele frequencies
keyTerms.quote: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration

keyTerms.gloss: group of members that breed primarily among themselves within a geographic area
keyTerms.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.

keyTerms.gloss: alternative classification to race for grouping human populations by ethnic origins
keyTerms.quote: An alternative to classifying the human species by race is to divide them by ethnicity.
